Two things:

1) Self-actualize. Decide what you value in life and what leaves you feeling accomplished. This will lead to a sense of self confidence and happiness derived from your own actions, which results in most slights rolling right off you like if a two year old insulted you (I mean really, someone who shits in their own pants mocking you will make you grin like a looby).

2) Stop being a whiny little bitch looking for an emotional tampon. The next time something upsets you, ask yourself "Did this person cause me substantial tangible harm in time/money/health/etc?" If not, tell yourself "IDGAF" and proceed to go do #1 even more than before.

Online's a bit different because everything is a lot more fake but also deliberate. Don't just consider what people say but why they're phrasing it the way they do. Somebody that's going extremely hostile and attacking you is likely to be young, extremely insecure, and often wants to believe something that they probably know deep down enough isn't true. If you truly believe what you're saying and have substantial logic behind it then going hostile makes no sense, since you know you're never going to convince anybody by calling them a bunch of insults. So just keep that in mind and act like a decent person while arguing your point. And you may end up giving them more to think about than their outward behavior would ever indicate.
